method: Reopened the claim-bearing public source passages for T131, T091, T097, T099 and T253. usedFacts.claim: The Mountainの自社史は、ベルト販売と1972年の初店舗を記す。
The Mountainの自社史は、Tシャツ工房の設立、店舗網、自社プリントTシャツ、および店舗売却後に印刷へ専念したと記す。年表の1991年表示と本文の1996年記載が一致しない。
The Mountainの自社史は、Three Wolf Moon後にBig Face動物Tシャツを始めたと記す。
NICENESSの公式商品ページはG.BERNARDのイメージソース、色別の重ね刷り、6.0oz、現行品のニカラグア製を説明している。

records.claimsStatus: The Mountain’s official timeline places its 30 retail locations in the 1972 section and the print shop in a separate 1976 section. The page does not date the 30-store milestone, so the article no longer implies the stores followed the print shop. Its 1996 prose and 1991 timeline heading remain explicitly discrepant.
records.independentReview: Pending. The author’s source recheck is not represented as independent editorial review.
records.editorialCorrection: Updated the headline and separated the 1976 print-shop account from the undated 30-store account; no unsupported order is stated.

usedFacts.claim: London Museum records cotton jeans bought by Kim Philpotts in the 1980s, made by Katharine Hamnett and dated 1980–1989.
The museum describes Philpotts’s preference for British women designers and notes that she also wore Levi’s 501s; this is one person’s wardrobe.
NICENESS says CHARLES references 1980s British denim trousers, uses a raised-back pattern, cotton denim and printed lining, and is made in Japan.

sourceChecks.verifiedClaim: Kim Philpotts bought Katharine Hamnett cotton jeans in the 1980s; object dated 1980–1989. Museum says she preferred British female designers and also wore Levi’s 501s.
Official page identifies a British 1980s denim-trouser reference, raised-back pattern, cotton denim, graphic lining and Made in Japan.
Retailer labels this CHARLES product 26AW; used only for season metadata.

records.claimsStatus: Selected claims confirmed. The museum object is one person’s purchase, not a typical British pattern; it does not identify CHARLES’s precise source or the object’s sewing location.
records.boundary: London Museum records one owner’s garment. The relationship to CHARLES is a brand-stated reference, not an object identification.
records.independentReview: Pending; source rechecking by the drafter is not independent editorial review.

usedFacts.claim: The Met describes Hiroshige’s ca.1833–34 Kuwana print as two boats approaching Kuwana port after a two-hour trip from Miya.
A separate Hiroshige Goyu print has visible credits naming Ichiryūsai, engraver Jirobei, printer Heibei and publisher Takenouchi, as the Met explains.
NICENESS says B.PALMER’s port-town landscape was inspired by the Tokaido Fifty-Three Stations and describes the current fabric’s Hokuriku weaving and Kyoto discharge printing.

sources.title: Station Forty-Three: Kuwana, Seven-Ri Ferry at the Port

sourceChecks.verifiedClaim: Met says foreground boats are about to reach Kuwana port after a two-hour journey from Miya; Hiroshige, ca.1833–34, woodblock print.
Met identifies the print credits including Ichiryūsai as a Hiroshige pseudonym, engraver Jirobei, printer Heibei and publisher Takenouchi.
Official page states port-landscape inspiration from Tokaido Fifty-Three Stations, current board-shirt construction and textile/print processes.

records.claimsStatus: Selected claims confirmed. No exact reference print, artist, station or individual image was attributed to B.PALMER. The Goyu print is a comparison source, not an identified garment source.
records.boundary: The Met works are comparison records, not identified B.PALMER originals. NICENESS does not name an exact print; print credits are not equated with current clothing production.

usedFacts.claim: Archie Green’s 2001 article describes Frisco jeans as straight-leg heavy black cotton twill and reports Ben Davis had made them in San Francisco since 1935.
The 1948 Labor Day parade caption identifies the SUP contingent’s outfit as white shirts, Frisco jeans and white caps.
Green quotes Joe Gladstone’s later recollection of an unofficial outfit associated with belonging to West Coast seafarers.
NICENESS says N.MORLEY uses a 1950s US Frisco trouser base with British trouser construction and a linen canvas carrying a scanned denim transfer print.

sources.title: Harry Lundeberg Stetson: A Centennial Tribute — p.3
sources.publisher: West Coast Sailors / Sailors’ Union of the Pacific

sourceChecks.verifiedClaim: Caption lists white shirts, Frisco jeans and Lundeberg stetsons for the 1948 parade. Article gives Green’s Frisco-jeans description, says outfit was unofficial and quotes Gladstone’s later recollection.
Official page states 1950s US Frisco trousers, British slacks construction, linen canvas with scanned 1950s denim transfer and Made in Japan.
Retail listing identifies N.MORLEY within its 26AW assortment; used only for season metadata.

records.claimsStatus: Selected claims confirmed. Green’s description is a 2001 retrospective, not a 1935 manufacturer catalog. The parade outfit is described as unofficial, and the exact date of any union mandate remains unknown. The 1948 comparison predates the stated 1950s product reference.
records.boundary: The photograph/caption and later recollection are bounded to their stated contexts; no universal sailor dress code, exact garment manufacturer from the photograph or direct NICENESS prototype is claimed.
records.independentReview: Pending; source rechecking by the drafter is not independent editorial review.

usedFacts.claim: The 1955 revision of DoD Instruction 4210.2 lists Flying Man’s Type N-2B in an Air Force textile-items table with wool/nylon and a MIL-J-6278-series specification.
NICENESS describes MARSH as a Japan-made cold-weather vest editing details seen on 1950s US N-2/N-3 flight jackets and other military garments.

sources.title: Department of Defense Instruction 4210.2, Change 1
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Defense / National Archives

sourceChecks.locator: Air Force textile items table, p.9
sourceChecks.verifiedClaim: The 1955 revision includes “Jacket, Flying Man’s Type N-2B”; the list records an item label, not a specific wearer or conditions.
Official page describes the Japan-made wool/nylon cold-weather vest, North American coyote fur and editing of N-2/N-3 and other military details.

records.claimsStatus: Existing research and validation hashes match. The government list establishes the item label; it does not identify MARSH’s direct source or specific issue/use.
records.boundary: The DoD list gives a type label, not a detailed garment or wear record. NICENESS names N-2/N-3 and various military details but does not identify N-2B as its direct source.
